product: Quincy 9-inch Antique Ocean Desk Globe - Walnut Finish Hardwood Base

entries.text: Hi, it's Mia from Replogle Globes. Thanks for taking a few minutes with me: your code, $20 off, shows up on screen as soon as we finish. I see you were looking at the Quincy 9-inch Antique Ocean Desk Globe - Walnut Finish Hardwood Base. What caught your eye?
I like the antique
styling.

The antique styling is lovely. I should tell you that this Quincy is sold out right now, though. The parchment-toned oceans give it that vintage look.

What's the globe for, and where would it go?
It's for me, it would go on a desk in my home.
A desk at home, lovely. When you're choosing something like this for yourself, what matters most to you?
Appearance and also accuracy of the globe.
Appearance and accuracy, got it. Have you had a globe before, or is this your first? I'd love to hear how that went.
I've had a globe before, but it was many years ago when I was a teenager.
That's a nice memory to come back to. What did you do with that globe back then, and what happened to it?
I would consult the Globe to learn more about geography, but I don't remember what happened to it.
Learning geography from it, that's great. Now that you're choosing one again, what else are you looking at besides Replogle Globes?

It's mostly just that brand. I wondered if I should get a twelve inch globe, but my concern when I'm looking at different lists is the quality. I'm not sure about the metal on some of the globes, if it is going to look like plastic.
Fair worry. I can't judge how the metal looks from here, but each product page lists the materials, like die-cast metal and solid hardwood. What would help you feel sure about the quality?
Reading reviews of people who have the globe or globes I'm looking at to know whether it looks like plastic or not.
Reading real owners' reviews makes sense for that. How did you first find Replogle Globes?
Internet search for Canadian sources for world globes.
Searching for a Canadian source, that makes sense. Aside from the globe itself, what do you like to buy regularly for your desk or home, and why?
I don't usually buy much from my desk. Actually. I have most of what I need that I acquired long ago, but a more recent purchase is a calendar, a perpetual calendar for my desk.
A perpetual calendar, nice choice. What made you pick that one, and roughly what did it cost you?

Cost me only about ten dollars. It's very small. And inexpensive overall. It's not fancy. I just wanted something simple that I, every day, could check the date with and move sliders on it. So it helps me remember the date because I actively have to change the calendar.
That's a thoughtful little habit, touching it each day. Is there anything you wish a desk globe did, or came with, that you haven't seen?

No. I don't think so because every globe I've looked at, I just like the old fashioned It spins. That's about all it does. I don't want it to be glow in the dark or yeah, I don't need any special features.
Simple and old-fashioned, that makes sense. Thank you so much for sharing all of this with me. Your code is coming up on your screen now. Goodbye!
